html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. SDK: software development kit; URL: uniform resource locator

  • The hub-and-spoke (coordinator and subagents) architecture and why all communication goes through the coordinator
  • Why subagents have isolated context and what that means for prompts
  • How the coordinator decomposes, delegates, aggregates and refines, and the risk of too narrow a decomposition
  • How to spawn subagents: the Task tool, allowedTools, AgentDefinition, parallel spawning, forks

2The Coordinator and Subagents

Running case

Birchwood Supply Researches a Market

  • Birchwood's analysts ask: "What is changing in home energy?"
  • A coordinator agent splits the question and hands parts to four subagents: web search, document analysis, synthesis and report generation
  • The final report must be complete and cited

In the hub-and-spoke pattern, one coordinator agent is the hub; the subagents are spokes.

The coordinator... Why it matters
Decomposes the task and decides which subagents to invoke from the query's complexity Simple questions should not run the full pipeline
Delegates with clear goals and passes the needed context Subagents do not share memory
Aggregates results and evaluates them for gaps Quality control sits in one place
Manages all communication, error handling and information routing Gives observability, consistent error handling and controlled information flow
  • Subagents operate with isolated context: they do not inherit the coordinator's conversation history.
  • Route every subagent exchange through the coordinator, not subagent to subagent.
Exam tip

"Why route communication through the coordinator?" → observability, consistent error handling, controlled information flow.

3Decomposition: Coverage and Dynamic Selection

  • Too narrow a decomposition is the classic failure. If the coordinator turns "home energy" into "rooftop solar", "solar inverters" and "solar financing", every subagent can do a perfect job and the report still misses batteries, heat pumps and wind. The root cause is the coordinator's task decomposition, not the downstream agents.
  • Design the coordinator to analyze the query's requirements and choose which subagents to invoke, instead of always running the whole pipeline.
  • Partition the scope to minimize duplication: give each agent a distinct subtopic or source type (for example "market data" versus "academic papers").
  • Use an iterative refinement loop: the coordinator checks the synthesis for gaps, re-delegates targeted queries to search and analysis agents, and re-invokes synthesis until coverage is sufficient.

Exam tip

When the final output has a missing area but each subagent "succeeded", look at how the coordinator split the task.

4Spawning Subagents (Task 1.3)

Element What to know
Spawning tool Subagents are started by the Task tool. For a coordinator to start them, allowedTools must include "Task"
AgentDefinition Each subagent type has a description (when to use it), a system prompt and tool restrictions
Context A subagent does not inherit the parent's context or share memory between invocations: put everything it needs in its prompt
Forks Fork-based session management creates branches to explore divergent approaches from a shared baseline (see Module 4)

[Old name] / [Verify live] In current Claude Code and Agent SDK documentation the spawning tool is named Agent; it was renamed from Task in Claude Code v2.1.63, and Task still works as an alias. The exam guide uses Task and allowedTools containing "Task". Answer with the guide's wording; in real code include both names or the current one. As of 8 November 2026.

research_agents = {
    "web-search": AgentDefinition(
        description="Finds recent web sources for a research subtopic.",
        prompt="You search the web and return findings as structured JSON.",
        tools=["WebSearch"]),
    "synthesis": AgentDefinition(
        description="Combines findings into a cited summary.",
        prompt="You merge the findings you are given and keep every citation.",
        tools=["verify_fact"]),     # narrow tool for a frequent need (Module 6)
}
options = ClaudeAgentOptions(allowed_tools=["Task"], agents=research_agents)

Passing context

  • Include complete findings from earlier agents directly in the next subagent's prompt (for example, the search results and the document analysis go into the synthesis prompt).
  • Use a structured format that separates content from metadata (claim, source URL, document name, page number, date) so attribution survives the hand-off.
  • Spawn in parallel by emitting several Task tool calls in one coordinator response, not across separate turns; parallel calls cut latency.
  • Write coordinator prompts that give the goal and the quality criteria, not a step-by-step procedure, so subagents can adapt.

[Verify live] Current documentation: a subagent's final message returns to the parent as a summary, so verbose intermediate work stays out of the parent's context; subagents can run in parallel and (by default) can themselves spawn subagents up to three levels below the main agent. As of 8 November 2026.

Exam tip

A subagent that "does not know" something almost always means the coordinator never put it in the prompt: subagents do not inherit context or memory.

5Exam Q&A

S1Birchwood's research system produces a report on "the future of home energy" that covers only solar power. Logs show each subagent finished successfully and the coordinator created three subtasks, all about solar panels. What is the most likely root cause?

  • AThe web search agent's queries were too short
  • BThe coordinator's task decomposition was too narrow
  • CThe document analysis agent filtered out battery and heat-pump sources
  • DThe synthesis agent lacks gap-detection instructions
Show the answer

Answer: B. The logs show the coordinator assigned only solar subtasks. The subagents did what they were assigned; the gap comes from the decomposition.

S2Which is the main reason to route all subagent communication through the coordinator?

  • ASubagents cannot communicate with each other in any multi-agent system, so the hub is mandatory
  • BIt makes every subagent run noticeably faster because they all share the same context
  • CIt removes the need for a system prompt
  • DObservability, consistent error handling and controlled information flow
Show the answer

Answer: D. The hub-and-spoke pattern centralizes monitoring, errors and routing in one place.

S3A coordinator always runs search, analysis, synthesis and reporting for every request, even a one-line factual question. What change is most appropriate?

  • ARemove the reporting subagent and let the search subagent write each answer
  • BForce every request through the pipeline twice
  • CLet it analyze the query and invoke only the subagents needed
  • DMake subagents call each other directly
Show the answer

Answer: C. A coordinator should select subagents dynamically based on complexity instead of always running the full pipeline.

S4The synthesis subagent produces summaries with missing citations. It receives only the instruction "combine the findings", while the coordinator holds the search results in its own conversation. What is the best fix?

  • AAsk the subagent to search again from scratch
  • BInclude the complete findings, with source URLs and document names in a structured format, in the synthesis subagent's prompt
  • CAssume the subagent can read the coordinator's conversation history and find the sources itself
  • DRaise max_tokens for the coordinator
Show the answer

Answer: B. Subagents do not inherit context; everything required, including attribution metadata, must be in the prompt.

S5A coordinator must delegate a search and a document analysis that do not depend on each other. How should it start them to minimize latency?

  • AMerge both jobs into one subagent prompt
  • BStart the analysis first and the search only if the analysis fails
  • CEmit both Task tool calls in a single response so they run in parallel
  • DStart the search, wait for the full result, then start the analysis in a later turn
Show the answer

Answer: C. Multiple Task calls in one coordinator response let independent subagents run in parallel.

S6A coordinator's allowedTools list contains only Read and Grep, and no subagent ever starts. What is missing?

  • AA larger context window
  • BA longer system prompt
  • CA Pydantic model that describes each subagent's output
  • DThe "Task" tool in allowedTools
Show the answer

Answer: D. To invoke subagents, the coordinator's allowedTools must include the Task tool (named Agent in current documentation).

S7Which coordinator prompt follows the recommended style?

  • A"Step 1: search exactly three named sites. Step 2: copy the first paragraph of each page. Step 3: stop and report."
  • B"Research the topic broadly; goal: a cited overview that covers all major sub-areas; quality: every claim has a source and gaps are named."
  • C"Do whatever seems right."
  • D"Use the same prompt for every subagent."
Show the answer

Answer: B. Specify goals and quality criteria so subagents can adapt, rather than a rigid procedure.

S8After synthesis, the coordinator notices that the report has no data on the Asian market. What should it do?

  • ARe-delegate targeted queries to search and analysis, then re-invoke synthesis
  • BAsk the synthesis agent to invent plausible figures
  • CPublish the report as it is and mention the missing Asian market in a footnote only
  • DEnd the run with an error
Show the answer

Answer: A. The iterative refinement loop re-delegates for gaps and repeats until coverage is sufficient.

S9A research subagent returns summaries without citations. Which TWO changes help most? Select TWO.

  • ALet subagents message one another directly to share citations
  • BRely on the subagent inheriting the coordinator's conversation
  • CDrop citations to save tokens
  • DRequire the subagent to output each claim together with its source metadata
  • EPut the findings, with source URLs and document names in a structured format, into the subagent's prompt
Show the answer

Answer: D, E. Subagents do not inherit context, so attribution must be passed in and must be produced as structured output. Peer messaging bypasses the coordinator and dropping citations loses provenance.

S10Which TWO are benefits of routing all subagent communication through the coordinator? Select TWO.

  • AConsistent error handling in one place
  • BFaster peer-to-peer messaging between subagents
  • CNo need to write prompts for subagents
  • DObservability of what each subagent did
  • ELower token use in every case
Show the answer

Answer: A, D. A central hub gives observability, consistent error handling and controlled information flow. It does not remove the need for prompts or guarantee lower token use.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Pattern Hub-and-spoke: coordinator + subagents; all communication via the coordinator
Why via coordinator Observability, consistent error handling, controlled information flow
Subagent context Isolated; does not inherit history or share memory; give it everything in its prompt
Spawning Task tool (now called Agent); allowedTools must include it; AgentDefinition = description + prompt + tool limits
Parallel Several Task calls in one coordinator response
Decomposition risk Too narrow → incomplete coverage though every subagent "succeeded"
Refinement loop Check gaps → re-delegate targeted queries → re-run synthesis until covered
Prompts Coordinator gives goals and criteria, not procedures; pass content + metadata in structured form
